standard_prerequisites.name: Comparability graph of a partially ordered set and the partition number p(G)
standard_prerequisites.statement: A comparability graph has an edge between two vertices exactly when the corresponding elements of a partially ordered set are comparable, and p(G) is the minimum number of edge-disjoint comparability subgraphs of G whose union is the whole edge set; retained at source lines 117-120 and 128.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted theorem asserts p(G) <= 2, so both the class of graphs used in the partition and the parameter bounded must be available.

standard_prerequisites.name: Generalized split graphs
standard_prerequisites.statement: A graph G is a GSP graph when either G or its complement can be written with its vertex set partitioned into V_1 and V_2, where V_1 is a complete graph and V_2 is a union of vertex-disjoint complete graphs with no edges between them; retained at source lines 204-206, and the article notes at source lines 208-209 that GSP graphs are perfect and form a subclass of the weakly triangulated graphs.
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the two structural cases of the proof, one for G itself and one for its complement, and the hypothesis of perfectness used in the second case.

core_obligations: Case one: assume the vertex set of the GSP graph G is partitioned into V_1 and V_2 with V_1 a complete graph and V_2 a union of vertex-disjoint complete graphs K_i and no edges between them (source lines 230-231).

Check that the complete subgraphs spanned by V_1 and by the vertex sets of the K_i form one comparability graph, and that the bipartite graph [V_1,V_2] of the edges between the two parts forms another, so that the two of them partition the edge set of G in this case (source lines 232-233).
Case two: assume instead that V_1 is an independent set of G and that V_2 spans a complete partite graph H (source lines 235-236).
Use that a complete partite graph is a comparability graph, take H as the first comparability graph, and take the bipartite graph spanned by [V_1,V(H)] in G as the second (source lines 236-237).
Combine the two cases, which cover a GSP graph and its complement, to conclude p(G) <= 2 for every GSP graph (source line 237).

proof_roadmap.step: Split a GSP graph according to the first structural alternative into a complete graph and a union of disjoint complete graphs.
Exhibit the two comparability graphs of the first case: the complete subgraphs and the bipartite graph between the two parts.
Handle the complementary alternative, where the first part is independent and the second spans a complete partite graph.
Take the complete partite graph and the bipartite graph between the parts as the two comparability graphs and conclude.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2408.13523v2 的 Theorem gensplit（源 225-226 行，证明 230-237 行，共 8 行）：对任意 GSP 图证明 p(G)<=2。证明的关键不是例行核验：GSP 的定义本身有两支（G 或其补图可剖成完全图与若干互不相连的完全图之并），证明必须对两支分别给出两个具体的可比图——第一支取「V_1 张成的完全子图与诸 K_i 的并」以及「两部分之间的二部图 [V_1,V_2]」（232-233 行），第二支取「V_2 张成的完全多部图 H」以及「[V_1,V(H)] 在 G 中的二部图」（235-237 行），并分别说明它们确实是可比图且边不交地覆盖整个边集。难点在于两种情形的分解方式不同、且必须各自验证两个分量都是可比图；原文位置在证明的 232-233 行与 236-237 行。

editorial_notes: The counted unit is the article's own Theorem gensplit at source lines 225-226 together with the author's proof that opens with the bold header Proof. at source line 230 and closes with the square at source line 237; the author separates the two by an introductory sentence at source line 222 and blank lines, so the pairing is by adjacency through those lines only.

The retained context at source lines 117-120 and 128-129 is the article's own description of comparability graphs and its definitions of p(G) and c(G); the retained context at source lines 204-206 and 208-209 is its own definition of a GSP graph and its own remark that GSP graphs are perfect and weakly triangulated. The sentences carrying the citations to Hayward and to the strong perfect graph theorem are deliberately not retained.

The source preamble cannot be retained as it stands: it loads rawfonts, psfrag, verbatim, tikz with several libraries, hyperref with the pagebackref option and a dvi driver option for graphicx, none of which the retained body spans use, and it redefines backref commands that only exist because of that hyperref option. The retained preamble file therefore carries, line for line, source line 2, source line 3, source line 4, source line 16, source line 17, the theorem declarations of source lines 20-30 and the author macro definitions of source lines 32-41; the only textual change anywhere is the removal of the dvipdfm driver option from the graphicx line, because the assembly forces the xelatex engine. No new macro, package or declaration was introduced.
No retained line contains a citation or a cross-reference, so the material carries no bibliography and needs no external navigation pointer.

The article's Theorem twocover, Theorem promelsteger, Theorem bipline, Theorem unit, Theorem co-triangulated, Theorem loglog, Theorem ub, Lemma rec, the corollaries genupbound, shift, doblesh and p', and Proposition H9 are not counted here.
